chunks.text:
Meloxicam is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID).
Meloxicam works by reducing hormones that cause pain, fever, and inflammation in the body.
Meloxicam is used to relieve pain, tenderness, swelling, and stiffness.
These symptoms are caused by osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis.
Osteoarthritis is arthritis caused by a breakdown of the lining of the joints.
Rheumatoid arthritis is arthritis caused by swelling of the lining of the joints.
Meloxicam is used to relieve pain, tenderness, swelling, and stiffness.
These symptoms are caused by juvenile rheumatoid arthritis.
Juvenile rheumatoid arthritis is a type of arthritis that affects children.
Meloxicam is used in children 2 years of age and older.
IV meloxicam (brands Anjeso [discontinued], Qamzova, Xifyrm) is used for moderate to severe pain in adults, alone or in combination with non-NSAID analgesics.
Vivlodex capsules [discontinued] are only for use in adults.
Qmiiz ODT (orally disintegrating tablet) [discontinued] is for adults and children weighing at least 132 pounds (60 kilograms).
Generic meloxicam is available.

chunks.text:
Meloxicam can increase your risk of a fatal heart attack or stroke.
This risk is especially high if you use Meloxicam long term.
The risk is also higher if you take high doses.
The risk is further increased if you have heart disease.
Even people without heart disease or risk factors could have a stroke or heart attack while taking Meloxicam.
Do not use Meloxicam just before or after heart bypass surgery (coronary artery bypass graft, or CABG).
Avoid taking meloxicam after a recent heart attack, unless your doctor tells you to.
You may have an increased risk of another heart attack if you take Meloxicam after a recent heart attack.
Get emergency medical help if you have chest pain, weakness, shortness of breath, slurred speech, or problems with vision or balance.
Meloxicam may also cause stomach or intestinal bleeding.
This bleeding can be fatal.
These conditions can occur without warning while you are using Meloxicam, especially in older adults.
Call your doctor at once if you have symptoms of stomach bleeding.
Such symptoms include black, bloody, or tarry stools.

chunks.text:
Pregnancy:
If you are pregnant, you should not take meloxicam unless your doctor tells you to.
Taking an NSAID at about 20 weeks of pregnancy or later may harm your unborn baby.
If you need to take Meloxicam for more than 2 days when you are between 20 and 30 weeks of pregnancy.
Your doctor may need to monitor the amount of fluid around your baby.
You should not take meloxicam after about 30 weeks of pregnancy.
Planning a pregnancy:
Meloxicam may cause a delay in ovulation (the release of an egg from an ovary).
You should not take Meloxicam if you are undergoing fertility treatment or are otherwise trying to get pregnant.
Breastfeeding:
Ask a doctor if it is safe to breastfeed while using Meloxicam.

Take Meloxicam exactly as prescribed by your doctor.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Use the lowest effective dose for your condition.
Meloxicam oral is taken by mouth.
Meloxicam injection (Qamzova, Xifyrm) is given as an intravenous bolus injection over 15 seconds.
A healthcare provider will give you this injection.
Your dose needs may change if you switch to a different brand, strength, or form of meloxicam.
Avoid medication errors by using only the medicine your doctor prescribes.
Meloxicam doses are based on weight (especially in children and teenagers).
Your dose needs may change if you gain or lose weight.
If you use this medicine long-term, you may need frequent medical tests.
Store oral suspension, tablets, or capsules at room temperature, away from moisture and heat.
Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use.

Usual Adult Dose of Meloxicam for Osteoarthritis:
Oral tablets are available.
Oral disintegrating tablets are available.
The initial dose of oral tablets is 7.5 mg orally once a day.
The maintenance dose of oral tablets is 15 mg orally once a day in patients requiring additional analgesia.
The maximum dose of oral tablets is 15 mg orally once a day.
The initial dose of oral capsules is 5 mg orally once a day.
The maintenance dose of oral capsules is 10 mg orally once a day in patients requiring additional analgesia.
The maximum dose of oral capsules is 10 mg orally once a day.
Use: For the relief of signs and symptoms of osteoarthritis pain
Usual Adult Dose of Meloxicam for Rheumatoid Arthritis:
Oral Tablets and Oral Disintegrating Tablets have an initial dose of 7.5 mg orally once a day.
The maintenance dose is 15 mg orally once a day in patients requiring additional analgesia.
The maximum dose is 15 mg orally once a day.
Use: For the relief of signs and symptoms of rheumatoid arthritis
Usual Adult Dose of Meloxicam IV for Pain:
30 mg IV bolus (over 15 seconds) once a day.

chunks.text:
The median time to meaningful pain relief was 2 to 3 hours in clinical trials.
A non-NSAID with a rapid onset may be used in combination with IV meloxicam.
Some patients may not experience adequate analgesia for the first 24 hours.
The lowest effective dose for the shortest duration possible consistent with individual treatment goals should be used.
Usual Pediatric Dose of Meloxicam for Juvenile Rheumatoid Arthritis:
Oral disintegrating tablets in children 60 kg or greater: 7.5 mg orally once a day.
Oral suspension in children 2 years and older: 0.125 mg/kg orally once a day (to a maximum dose of 7.5 mg/day).
No additional benefit has been demonstrated with doses above 7.5 mg/day.
Oral formulations have not shown equivalent systemic exposure.
They are not considered interchangeable.
The oral disintegrating tablets should not be used in children who weigh less than 60 kg.

chunks.section_heading: What should I avoid while receiving meloxicam?
chunks.text:
Drinking alcohol may increase your risk of stomach bleeding.
Avoid taking aspirin while you are taking meloxicam, unless your doctor tells you to.
Ask a doctor or pharmacist before using other medicines for pain, fever, swelling, or cold/flu symptoms.
Other medicines may contain ingredients similar to meloxicam.
These ingredients include aspirin, ibuprofen, ketoprofen, or naproxen.

chunks.text:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to meloxicam.
Signs of an allergic reaction to meloxicam include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of a heart attack or stroke.
These signs include chest pain spreading to your jaw or shoulder.
These signs include sudden numbness or weakness on one side of the body.
These signs include slurred speech.
These signs include leg swelling.
These signs include feeling short of breath.
Meloxicam may cause serious side effects.
Stop using Meloxicam and call your doctor at once if you have:
the first sign of any skin rash, no matter how mild;
shortness of breath (even with mild exertion);
swelling or rapid weight gain;
signs of stomach bleeding - bloody or tarry stools, coughing up blood or vomit that looks like coffee grounds;

Common meloxicam side effects may include:
stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, heartburn
diarrhea, constipation, gas;
dizziness; or
cold symptoms, flu symptoms.
